deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a philosophical and physical draft belonging to Riemann's Naturphilosophie fragments (the Fechner-inspired 'Erdseele' discussion on the previous page, and the aether-flux theory of gravitation).

(a) The first line finishes the sentence begun on the previous page: from the standpoint of exact natural science, an Earth-soul is 'a hypothesis to explain the existence and the historical development of the organic world.'

(b) A new section begins, headed '2) über das Wesen[?]'. Riemann posits: 'Thinking is a process in the interior of ponderable matter.' He then deletes a first enumeration: (1) our own inner perception, (2) the known laws of action of ponderable matter on ponderable matter. He replaces it with: the facts of our outer perception that must be explained by processes inside ponderable (gravitating) matter are (1) universal gravitation and (2) the general laws of motion.

(c) Inner side. Every act of thought rests on something permanent. This shows itself as such only on special occasions, through memory, without exerting an immediate lasting influence on phenomena. So with each act of thought something permanent enters our soul, and it does exert a lasting influence on phenomena. This is the known doctrine that 'mit jedem einfachen Denkact tritt etwas Bleibendes, Substantielles in unsere Seele ein'.

(d) Outer side. Our outer experiences of ponderable matter can be explained if one assumes the following:
- the whole infinite space is filled with a homogeneous substance;
- this substance continually flows into ponderable matter and disappears there.

Riemann struck out a qualifier, roughly 'and indeed equal amounts in equal times'. That qualifier would hint at a constant flux proportional to mass.

The implicit physics is my reconstruction, not on the page. A steady, isotropic inflow into a point sink of strength proportional to mass m gives an inflow speed v = Q/(4*pi*r^2), i.e. proportional to m/r^2. This reproduces Newton's inverse-square law. The page gives no formula; the next page elaborates the medium's resistance to volume change and to change of length.

results.what: Hypothesis that space is filled with a homogeneous medium flowing continuously into ponderable matter and vanishing there, as the cause of gravitation (and with it the laws of motion)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann himself (published posthumously in Werke 1876, 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', 1853); related ideas from Euler and later Bjerknes

results.what: Each act of thought deposits something permanent in the soul; thinking is a process inside ponderable matter
Earth-soul as a hypothesis explaining the historical development of organic life
results.usually_credited_to: G. T. Fechner (Zend-Avesta, 1851); Riemann's discussion is published in Werke

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's well-known and published Naturphilosophie fragments (aether influx into ponderable matter; 'etwas Bleibendes' entering the soul with each act of thought). It contains no mathematics and nothing that is not already attributed to him.

checkable.asserts: Steady inflow of strength Q into a point sink through spheres of radius r gives speed Q/(4*pi*r^2) (flux conservation). This is the inverse-square behaviour implicit in the influx hypothesis; it is my reconstruction, not on the page.

transcription_corrections: First line should read 'geschichtlichen Entwicklung der organischen Welt.' (genitive, completing the sentence 'Erklärung des Daseins und der ...' from the previous page).
'unmittelbaren' is an interlinear insertion above 'dauernden' in the phrase 'ohne einen ... dauernden Einfluss'; the transcription is correct in substance.
The struck phrase before 'Jedem Denkact' reads approximately 'Unsere innere Wahrnehmung führt uns zu der Annahme, dass'.
In the last paragraph the word after 'dass' before 'den ganzen unendlichen Raum' appears to be a struck or overwritten word (possibly 'durch'), not a clear insertion.
Heading '2) über das Wesen[?]' remains uncertain.
